Shenzhen深圳

Youngest stock in the country, and the most finance-driven buyer pool.

Median asking
¥65k–115k/m²
Gross yield
1.4%–1.8%
Purchase cap
One self-use home
Land term
70 years, residential

Shenzhen grew from a fishing town to a megacity in forty years, and its housing stock shows it: most of what you can buy was built after 2000, with better layouts, lifts and management than older cities can offer.

The foreign community is smaller than Shanghai's but highly concentrated: Shekou and Sea World for families, Futian and Nanshan for finance and technology, and a growing Korean and Japanese presence in the east.

Can a foreigner buy here?

One self-use home. One year of work or study in Shenzhen, purchase inside Shenzhen, valid residence permit and employment proof. Expect the local housing bureau to verify social insurance or tax records.

Apartments in Shekou and Nanshan dominate. Villa compounds exist but are scarce and priced accordingly.

Before you view anything here

The paragraph above is a summary, not an answer. City practice is applied at district level and changes without much notice.

Take it to the counter: ask the district housing bureau to confirm your eligibility in writing, using the script in how to verify.

How to check it

Where to live

Districts that work for foreign buyers

Not every district is workable at every stage. These are the ones with the schools, services and resale liquidity foreigners actually need.

Shekou蛇口

The expatriate heartland: international schools, the ferry to Hong Kong, walkable streets and a settled foreign community.

Futian福田

CBD, best metro coverage, most central. Smaller units and higher prices per square metre.

Nanshan南山

Technology employers, coastal views, strong schools. The most competitive bidding outside Futian.

Luohu罗湖

Older, denser, closest to the Hong Kong border. Better value, older buildings.

Bao'an宝安

Newer stock and airport access, popular with buyers who accept a longer commute.

The market

How Shenzhen actually trades

New-build launches are frequent and often sold in phases with escalating pricing. Resale in Shekou and Nanshan is the most liquid segment for foreign buyers.

Living here

Settling in

Humid subtropical climate, excellent air quality by Chinese standards, and easy access to Hong Kong for flights and schooling. A one-hour ferry or a short train ride changes what services you have access to.

Know before you offer

Three risks in this market

  • Urban village (城中村) redevelopment timelines are politically driven and can stall for years.
  • Some newer stock is sold with restricted resale windows — confirm the certificate date, not the handover date.
  • Summer humidity punishes poorly maintained buildings; inspect for damp and air-conditioning age.

Best suited to

Buyers who want modern stock, a compact foreign community, and proximity to Hong Kong.

Structure of a deal

What a purchase in Shenzhen actually looks like

Price is the last thing that decides the outcome. These four decide it first, and every one of them can be checked before you sign anything.

Who is on the other side

The marginal buyer is a technology or finance employee carrying leverage, so lending rules move their budget more than sentiment does. Reference-price policy can cap a mortgage below the contract price, which means a buyer may need cash for the gap.

What actually trades

Most stock was built after 2000, with better lifts and management than older cities can offer. New launches arrive in phases with rising prices, so the phase you can actually buy is often the worst-value one.

What is normal to negotiate

Ask for the certificate date rather than the handover date, because restricted resale windows run from the certificate. If the seller needs your money to clear their mortgage, that is a scheduling risk to price, not a discount to enjoy.

What your exit looks like

Shekou and Nanshan resell; urban-village redevelopment and peripheral new supply do not. Check how many units in the compound are rented out, since a rental-heavy building sells slowly regardless of price.

The four words a city is argued in

  • 限购Purchase restriction
  • 学区School catchment
  • 契税Deed tax
  • 满五唯一Five years, only home
